whyThisFails.theFormItselfPrintsTheDisambiguatorOnOne: Rendered the delivered canonical page 1 and read it: the question-1 charge table on 200-00130 prints '1.', '2.' and '3.' down its left margin, one per row. The committed field map already carries those printed numbers - production-field-map.json requiredBeforeFiling gives printedContext '1.' for fields 1/2/3, '2.' for 4/5/6 and '3.' for 7/8/9. The form offers a printed distinguisher for nine of these blanks, the map has already read it out of the pinned binary, and the delivered list drops it.

aSecondFindingInTheSameArtifact.name: Two rows of the 200-00132 table are emitted in reverse reading order, so a demonstrative precedes its antecedent
aSecondFindingInTheSameArtifact.whatTheDeliveredPageSays: In the `### 200-00132` table the row 'Address (other state entities to notify) | that agency's address' is printed ABOVE 'State Agency (other state entities to notify) | the name of any other state agency the court should notify, if you know of one'. It happens twice, for both rows of that block. A participant reading down the list meets 'that agency's address' before any agency has been named.
aSecondFindingInTheSameArtifact.measuredCause: The list is ordered by descending y and ignores x. On 200-00132 page 1 the two blanks of each notify row sit on ONE printed line: State Agency at x=53.17 y=356.30 and Address at x=254.61 y=356.35 - 0.05 pt apart in y, and the right-hand blank sorts first. The second pair is State Agency x=53.97 y=340.06 and Address x=254.30 y=341.28, 1.22 pt apart, and flips the same way.
aSecondFindingInTheSameArtifact.whyTheOtherFormIsFine: The identical block on 200-00130 page 2 has State Agency at y=565.62 and Address at y=563.66 - 1.96 pt apart, enough for the y-sort to land them in printed order. So the defect is not systemic ordering; it is a tie-break failure that appears only where two side-by-side blanks are within about 1.2 pt of each other.
aSecondFindingInTheSameArtifact.confirmedVisually: Rendered boundary page 3 and read it. The form prints the 'State Agency' column heading on the left and 'Address' on the right, exactly as the rects say. The delivered list reverses them.
aSecondFindingInTheSameArtifact.scope: 4 of the 46 rows. It is recorded here rather than as a separate failed obligation because it is the same artifact and the same rendering step as the failure above, and a repair to that step should fix both.

SERVICE.measured: The participant serves no process. The instructions and the guidance page both say so and both give the mechanism: on the petition route the court provides a copy to the prosecutor; on the stipulated route the participant takes or sends the signed stipulation to the prosecuting office and the prosecutor signs and files it. That matches the registry. There is no service step the packet asks the participant to perform and none it omits.
SERVICE.openLegalQuestionRecordedNotResolved: The committed registry carries a release blocker on affectedElement notice_or_service: whether victims receive notice on the Sec. 7603(a)(1) court-initiated route, since 13 V.S.A. Sec. 7608 requires the respondent to notify a known victim at the time a petition is filed and by its terms that duty does not attach where no petition is filed. The packet's participant-facing text does not mention victim notice on any route. That is not a misstatement of the participant's own service obligation - the duty, where it attaches, is the respondent's - so it does not fail this obligation. It is recorded here because the participant filing a petition is the case where the registry reads the duty as attaching, and what the participant is told to expect is a counsel question already open in the record.
